documents.abstract: CT Perfusion in Acute Ischemic Stroke Beyond 4.5 Hours: Extending Thrombectomy Window Using Core-Penumbra Mismatch — V1 Synthetic Educational Model Highlighting Collateral Variability and Need for Indian Validation of AI Trained on Foreign Data Authors: Kishore Das (Independent Researcher – Biomedical Engineer, Madhyamgram, Kolkata, India ) Keywords: CT Perfusion, CTP, Core Penumbra Mismatch, Acute Ischemic Stroke, Collateral Circulation, AI Bias, Indian Population, Synthetic Educational Model, Thrombectomy Window, Imaging Biomarker Abstract: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) due to large vessel occlusion (LVO) causes rapid neuronal death. Intravenous thrombolysis is limited to 4.5 hours, but in India >90% patients present late after 8-12 hours. Objective: 1) To explain CTP physics, 2) To show how CTP extends window from 4.5 hr to 24 hr using Core-Penumbra mismatch, 3) To highlight potential AI bias when AI Trained on Foreign Data auto-perfusion software is applied to Indian population. Methods: This V1 is 100% synthetic educational model only. No patient data, no real CTP scans. All figures are schematic. Protocol: Step 1 NCCT Head to exclude hemorrhage, Step 2 CTA Head and Neck to see LVO ICA/M1, Step 3 CTP. Parameters: 40-50 ml contrast at 5 ml/sec, 60-70 sec scanning at 80 kVp. Four maps: CBF <30% = Core (Dead Brain - Blue Center), CBV low in Core, MTT >6 sec = Penumbra, Tmax >6 sec = Penumbra (At-Risk - Red Yellow Around). Results: Illustrative Hypothetical Synthetic Case (100% Educational - No Real Patient): *Concept: - Core <70 ml = Dead part small - operation possible - Penumbra = At Risk Part - can be saved - Mismatch Ratio = Penumbra / Core >1.8 = Savable part 1.8 times bigger than dead - good - Mismatch Volume >15 ml = At least 15 ml savable tissue must be there *Hypothetical Example (Synthetic Only): A hypothetical patient presents after 8 hours. NCCT Head is normal (plain black-white CT shows nothing common in early stroke). CTP shows Core 25 ml (dead brain part small blue in center cannot be saved) and Penumbra 110 ml (at risk big red-yellow around can be saved if blood returns quickly). Ratio = 110/25 = 4.4 which means savable 4 times more than dead. So even after 8 hours, thrombectomy (clot removal operation) can be done. *Note: This is 100% synthetic schematic calculation for teaching only, not a real case. Simple Tree Example: Core is dry dead tree in middle (Dead - cannot save). Penumbra is green trees around it drying but still alive (Can be saved if water / blood given quickly). Where AI is Used: CT detector hardware -> DAS -> CPU/GPU runs AI to make auto maps (RAPID type). Software reported trained on more than 50 perfusion studies from multiple sites (manufacturer reports larger internal datasets; we mention more than 50 with scientific caution). Since training mainly on AI Trained on Foreign Data, bias MAY exist for Indian pattern. Therefore, AI Trained on Foreign Data may need local Indian validation. V2 will test with real de-identified cases with IRB approval. Conclusion: CTP with Core-Penumbra mismatch can extend window from 4.5 hr to 24 hr and opens platform for next-generation medicine design. Introduction: AIS is sudden block in brain artery due to clot. This V1 is 100% CT based for practical Indian emergency use (Fast 5 min, available in 90% hospitals, low cost 4000-6000 Rs) as per DEFUSE-3 and DAWN which extended window to 24 hours. Tree Example: Core is dry dead tree in middle (cannot save). Penumbra is green trees around it drying but alive. Discussion - Drug Design and Development Vision: Educational Note: All investigational agents mentioned below are cited solely as EXAMPLES OF INVESTIGATIONAL DRUG DESIGN CLASSES to illustrate how CTP can serve as quantitative imaging biomarker / measurement tool in future trials as per FDA guidance on enrichment criteria where CTP mismatch is used as inclusion criteria. No dosage, no formulation, no route, no efficacy, no safety, no promotional claim is made. No commercial product is endorsed. This V1 is synthetic educational model only. 1. Need for New Medicine: Current standard thrombolytic works only within 4.5 hours, after that bleeding risk high. 2. New Medicine Classes Under Design (Examples only): - Class 1: Next-generation single-bolus thrombolytics (Example molecule class: tenecteplase-type plasminogen activators) - Class 2: Neuroprotectants / Cell-death pathway inhibitors (Example molecule class: PSD-95 inhibitor type such as NA-1 class agents) - Class 3: Anti-reperfusion injury modulators (Post-recanalization edema/inflammation modulators) 3. How CTP Helps Testing: CTP shows Core and Penumbra. So medicine developer can test if new medicine reduces Core growth and saves Penumbra. FDA uses CTP mismatch for new medicine testing as inclusion tool. 4. AI + Medicine Design: AI can predict which Penumbra will become Core without vs with medicine. For Indian population, dose may need adjustment. So Indian CTP database is needed. 5. Importance: 24 hour window is golden time for new medicine delivery. *Researcher Explanation for Figure 5: Collateral circulation means network of small vessels that provide alternative blood flow when main artery is blocked. Limitations: V1 is synthetic only. No real CTP scans. All schematic. Values from literature (DEFUSE-3, DAWN). V2 will have real de-identified cases with IRB approval. Conclusion: CTP with Core and Penumbra mismatch can extend window from 4.5 hr to 24 hr. Indian population needs local validation of AI Trained on Foreign Data. Ethics Statement: All images synthetic educational, no patient data, no consent needed for V1. No human or animal study. No funding. Disclosures: No conflict of interest. No financial support. Abbreviations: AIS: Acute Ischemic Stroke – Sudden block in brain artery due to clot AI: Artificial Intelligence – Computer software that learns from data to make maps CBF: Cerebral Blood Flow – How much blood is going per minute – <30% means Core CBV: Cerebral Blood Volume – How much blood is stored – Low in Core CT: Computed Tomography – X-ray based scan machine CTA: CT Angiography – CT of blood vessels to see block CTP: CT Perfusion – Special CT that measures blood flow map with colors DAS: Data Acquisition System – Digital converter DAWN: DWI or CTP Assessment with Clinical Mismatch in the Triage of Wake-Up and Late Presenting Strokes Undergoing Neurointervention, AI Trained on Foreign Data trial that extended window to 24 hours DEFUSE-3: Endovascular Therapy Following Imaging Evaluation for Ischemic Stroke 3 – AI Trained on Foreign Data trial that extended window to 16 hours FDA: Food and Drug Administration ICA: Internal Carotid Artery - Big artery in neck supplying brain IRB: Institutional Review Board / Ethics Committee LVO: Large Vessel Occlusion – Block in big artery M1: M1 Segment of Middle Cerebral Artery – First part of main brain artery MTT: Mean Transit Time – How much time blood takes to pass – >6 sec means Penumbra NCCT: Non-Contrast CT – Plain black and white CT to see bleeding PSD-95: Postsynaptic Density Protein 95 – Brain protein involved in cell-death signaling RAPID: Rapid Processing of Perfusion and Diffusion – Automated software type that draws color maps Tmax: Time to Maximum – Delay in blood reaching – >6 sec means Penumbra References: 1. DEFUSE 3 Trial, NEJM 2018 2. DAWN Trial, NEJM 2018 3. AHA/ASA Guidelines - CTP recommended for extended window 4. FDA 510k RAPID - Auto core volume measurement 5. Menon BK, Stroke 2013 - Collateral variability 6. Liebeskind DS, Stroke 2003 - Collateral concept 7. Indian stroke registry

Tree Example: Core is dry dead tree in middle (cannot save). Penumbra is green trees around it drying but alive. Sierra Leone is faced with complex energy challenges, including very low rates of access to electricity. Nevertheless, ambitious goals have been set for the country through the Energy Transition and Green Growth Plan. Opportunities for solar energy deployment feature prominently in these goals, although they are clearly imagined in very different ways by the various energy sector actors. Some see large-scale hydropower as the future backbone of the electricity system, with opportunities for deploying solar photovoltaic energy in an auxiliary role. Others emphasise the potential of solar mini-grids. Still others see the greatest potential in household-scale solar systems to meet basic energy needs. In this article, we use the concept of sociotechnical imaginaries to examine these competing narratives. We argue that all of these technologies have their place in the future energy landscape of the country, but the vastly different geographical and economic realities and needs of diverse communities need to be duly considered when shaping the future energy landscape.

Multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models (LLMs) have converged on a common assumption: that the communication topology connecting agents is either fixed at design time or left entirely to unconstrained dynamic negotiation. This paper argues, through a heuristic reading of seven recent arXiv preprints spanning cs.MA, cs.DC, and cs.NI, that this binary is a false dichotomy, and that the most effective systems in the corpus share a structural pattern we call deliberate topology selection: the explicit, policy-guided choice of which edges to activate, suppress, or reconfigure at runtime, conditioned on task state, budget, and agent confidence. This is a heuristic reading, not a derivation from a shared formalism; the papers do not share a unified mathematical framework, but they converge on a common engineering diagnosis. The synthesis draws on findings about: training-free communication pruning via Theory-of-Mind confidence signals (arXiv:2605.29612) (a preprint its authors withdrew on 2026-09-22, so its reported results are not relied on here; see the Correction note); task-conditioned structural priors that guide posterior orchestration (arXiv:2605.25746); nucleus-electron hierarchies that separate stable backbones from dynamically activated agents (arXiv:2605.26178); game-theoretic minimax method selection under scenario uncertainty (arXiv:2606.02383); decentralized event-triggered synchronization under censored feedback (arXiv:2605.27076); federated market-based allocation over tree-structured service DAGs (arXiv:2605.27106); and infrastructure-layer topology proposals for V2X safety communication (arXiv:2605.25431). The central falsification path is concrete: if a static, task-agnostic topology trained once on a broad corpus consistently matches or outperforms deliberate topology selection across coordination-heavy benchmarks, the thesis collapses. The abstract reports no such result in any corpus paper; the claim remains a candidate structural pattern worth investigating, not an established law. Its authors have withdrawn that preprint, stating: "We identified a potential issue in the repeated-run evaluation of our method that may have caused unintended prompt overlap across runs and affected the reported results. We therefore withdraw the manuscript for further investigation and re-evaluation". Every claim that rested on CONCAT is removed, the count of synthesised findings drops from 7 to 6, and the topology-adaptation argument now rests on two papers only (DynaGraph and AgensFlow), which makes it weaker than version 2 presented it. A recurring structural pattern across recent multi-agent systems (MAS) research is that the mechanism by which agents reach collective decisions, aggregation versus deliberation, produces systematically different reliability and scalability profiles, and that neither mechanism dominates unconditionally. This paper synthesises 6 findings from recent arXiv preprints spanning cs.MA, cs.DC, and cs.NI to argue that this divergence is not incidental but is rooted in three interacting properties: (1) error correlation among agents, (2) the topology through which agents exchange information, and (3) the degree to which feedback signals are censored or delayed. We treat this as a heuristic reading across mechanistically distinct systems, not a derivation from a shared formal structure; the pattern is proposed, not proven. The core finding from prediction market oracle evaluation (arXiv:2605.30802) is the sharpest anchor: independent aggregation with confidence-weighted voting outperforms deliberative consensus, which degrades below single-model baselines, because deliberation propagates confident errors across agents whose outputs are already correlated (r = 0.529-0.689). This failure mode recurs in credit assignment for multi-agent prompt optimisation (arXiv:2605.30227) and in the censored-feedback coordination problem (arXiv:2605.27076). Complementary evidence from federated edge-cloud orchestration (arXiv:2605.27106) and dynamic topology reconfiguration (arXiv:2605.29511) suggests, by structural analogy, not direct equivalence, that topology-adaptive routing can recover coordination quality that static deliberation loses. The incremental voter model (arXiv:2605.28984) provides a mean-field analytic baseline for understanding how step-wise opinion updating in a fully-mixed topology converges or fails to converge under persuader bias; its connection to LLM deliberation is analogical and is treated as a weakly-connected addendum. The falsification path for the central claim is concrete: construct a benchmark where agent error correlation is experimentally varied from near-zero to near-one while holding task difficulty constant; if deliberative consensus degrades monotonically with correlation while aggregation does not, the mechanism is confirmed. If both degrade similarly, the topology assumption is the confound. Authorship: Saluca Agentic AI Research Team (Saluca LLC). This study examines the role, educational opportunities, and current challenges of integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies into higher education to develop university students' oral communication and foreign language speaking skills. Utilizing natural language processing (NLP), automatic speech recognition (ASR), and large language models (LLMs), the paper establishes a theoretical and practical framework for AI-mediated instruction. Key benefits, such as reducing foreign language speaking anxiety, constructing personalized learning trajectories, offering real-time corrective feedback, and enhancing phonetic accuracy and oral fluency, are analyzed in detail. Furthermore, the paper highlights critical implementation barriers and provides actionable pedagogical guidelines for incorporating AI applications effectively into tertiary curricula.

documents.abstract: This conceptual review examines how digital transformation is reshaping Indian commerce and the world of work that sustains it. Adopting an integrative literature review design, the study synthesises 30 scholarly and institutional sources, comprising foundational theory on technology and organisations, recent evidence on automation and artificial intelligence, and India-focused research and official reports on digitalisation, employment, informality and leadership, through thematic analysis. Four themes emerge: the digitalisation of commercial activity, the recomposition of employment, the centrality of workforce capability and leadership, and the risk of a widening divide between the organised economy and traditional and unorganised sectors. Official estimates place India's digital economy at 11.74% of national income in 2022-23, with a projected share of nearly one-fifth by 2029-30, which underlines the scale of the shift. The synthesis indicates that the employment effects of digitalisation are compositional and not uniformly negative, that returns to digital investment depend on complementary human and organisational capabilities, and that the informal workforce, including handloom producers, construction labour and migrant workers, remains largely outside the digital dividend. The paper integrates these insights into a Digital Commerce–Work–Capability framework and advances five research propositions for empirical testing. It offers practical guidance for business managers, educational institutions and policymakers seeking inclusive digital growth.

The processes in audit firms face operational challenges due to the reliance on manual workflows, particularly in managing audit engagement tasks and tracking auditor training hours. Such inefficiencies lead to an increased administrative burden and potential compliance risks. This work describes our initiatives to address these issues by developing a system that combines a web application to streamline audit engagement monitoring and a mobile application to monitor staff training. Initially designed to replace manual workflows, the system has evolved to incorporate generative artificial intelligence to enhance knowledge retrieval for audit-related queries. The initiatives improve the efficiency of audit engagement and staff training monitoring, enabling audit firms to achieve significant improvements in their workflow.

Ground deformation induced by the touchdown impact of collapsed bodies can adversely affect critical structures and facilities, including adjacent buildings, underground pipelines, and metro tunnels. This study investigates the soil deformation induced by collapsed body impact in two typical strata, namely homogeneous soil and stiff-over-soft strata. We conducted model tests for both strata, and established an experimentally validated numerical model using the LS-DYNA finite element analysis software. We analysed the dynamic response characteristics and energy dissipation patterns of both homogeneous soil and stiff-over-soft strata models under the most unfavorable working conditions of touchdown impact loading. Two methods, namely the force–displacement curve method and the Winkler foundation model, were adopted to predict the energy dissipation during the touchdown impact process. Research findings indicated that the dynamic response characteristics of homogeneous soil models under touchdown impact loading were significantly influenced by distance and depth. The majority (approximately 83.37%) is of the impact energy dissipated through plastic deformation of the soil. In stiff-over-soft strata, due to the confinement effect and ’shell effect’ of the concrete slab, localised failure and crack propagation within the slab dominate system energy dissipation, accounting for approximately 61.63% of the total impact energy. When employing force–displacement curves to predict energy dissipation in models directly subjected to impact, both models demonstrated good agreement with simulation results. However, when using the Winkler foundation model to predict energy dissipation in directly impacted models, the homogeneous soil model showed superior agreement. These findings can provide a valuable reference for the safety assessment and the formulation of protective measures for engineering structures affected by the touchdown impact loading of collapsed bodies.

This study establishes a rigorous mathematical and empirical framework governing the transient state-space deviations from deterministic logical trajectories---conceptually designated as temporary cognitive lapses---observed in Large Language Models (LLMs) under extended context horizons. Grounded in a functionalist paradigm that transitions human-AI interaction into a single, closed-loop symbiotic informatics matrix, we define these lapses as volatile log-probability fluctuations triggered by localized attention hyperpolarization across supersaturated symbolic fields. Unlike permanent structural hallucinations, the real-time injection of human-guided subsegmentation commands operates as an exogenous homeostatic forcing operator---termed a cognitive pulse. This external impulse perturbs the key-value (KV) cache history matrix via entry-wise Hadamard modulation, forcing an exact singular value condensation that flattens distorted log-probability landscapes. Consequently, the diffuse probability mass is compressed, executing an instantaneous non-continuous vertical trajectory jump that re-orients the hidden representation vectors back onto canonical factual state attractors. We provide quantitative theoretical predictions tracking these transitions across all operational co-evolutionary interaction phases, establishing a rigorous mathematical baseline for co-evolutionary intelligence survival. Global Identifier Code: CO-EVOLUTIONARY-COGNITIVE-LAPSE-RECOVERY-VIA-EXOGENOUS-ASYMMETRIC-HOMEOSTASIS-PULSE

Este ensayo examina la discrepancia entre la alfabetización técnica en inteligencia artificial y la preservación del juicio deliberativo, introduciendo el concepto de analfabetismo de agencia. Frente a marcos normativos como el Artículo 4 del Reglamento de Inteligencia Artificial de la Unión Europea, se analiza la falacia del «human-in-the-loop» como un mecanismo de legitimación burocrática y exculpación jurídica mediante el análisis empírico del sistema MCAS del Boeing 737 MAX. Finalmente, se proponen dos salvaguardas operativas indispensables para el autogobierno sociotécnico: la reserva operacional y el oficio de responder. ---This essay examines the gap between technical artificial intelligence literacy and the preservation of deliberative judgment, introducing the concept of agency illiteracy. In light of regulatory frameworks such as Article 4 of the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, it analyzes the fallacy of the "human-in-the-loop" as an instrument of bureaucratic legitimation and legal exculpation through the empirical case of the Boeing 737 MAX MCAS system. Finally, it proposes two indispensable operational safeguards for sociotechnical self-governance: operational reserve and the craft of answering (moral accountability).
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Este trabajo formaliza el ensayo de suficiencia como un protocolo de auditoría sociotécnica concebido para verificar la autonomía operativa y el discernimiento deliberativo en entornos de alta mediación computacional. Frente a métricas convencionales que premian la velocidad del binomio humano–máquina bajo asistencia ininterrumpida, se fundamenta el principio de «evaluación por sustracción» con salvaguardas explícitas de contención de riesgo. Se reelabora la noción de competencia parasitaria no como una deficiencia individual o culposa del operador, sino como una propiedad emergente de configuraciones institucionales que incentivan la delegación epistémica y restringen el acceso a los fundamentos del sistema. A partir de los marcos de la ingeniería de resiliencia (Hollnagel, Woods) y de la práctica de la ingeniería del caos ya consolidada en sistemas distribuidos, el ensayo desarrolla un protocolo estructurado en cuatro vectores normativos —continuidad esencial, degradación comprensible, suficiencia material y agencia verificable—, contextualiza el caso histórico del MCAS en la aviación civil como referencia documental sobre asimetría informativa y degradación inadvertida, y propone criterios de gobernanza aplicables a proyectos e infraestructuras críticas. ---This paper formalizes the "sufficiency test" as a sociotechnical auditing protocol designed to verify operational autonomy and deliberative judgment in highly mediated computational environments. In contrast to conventional performance metrics that reward human–machine throughput under continuous algorithmic assistance, it operationalizes the principle of "evaluation by subtraction" within explicit containment boundaries. The concept of parasitic competence is redefined not as an individual moral or technical failing, but as an emergent property of sociotechnical configurations that incentivize epistemic offloading while restricting structural access and deliberative authority. Grounded in resilience engineering frameworks (Hollnagel, Woods) and in the already-established practice of chaos engineering in distributed systems, the essay formulates a structured testing protocol across four normative vectors—essential continuity, understandable degradation, material sufficiency, and verifiable agency—, examines the MCAS civil aviation case as an illustrative documentary reference on information asymmetry and unannounced degradation, and outlines governance mechanisms for critical infrastructure and project management.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

In contrast to conventional performance metrics that reward human–machine throughput under continuous algorithmic assistance, it operationalizes the principle of "evaluation by subtraction" within explicit containment boundaries. The concept of parasitic competence is redefined not as an individual moral or technical failing, but as an emergent property of sociotechnical configurations that incentivize epistemic offloading while restricting structural access and deliberative authority. Grounded in resilience engineering frameworks (Hollnagel, Woods) and in the already-established practice of chaos engineering in distributed systems, the essay formulates a structured testing protocol across four normative vectors—essential continuity, understandable degradation, material sufficiency, and verifiable agency—, examines the MCAS civil aviation case as an illustrative documentary reference on information asymmetry and unannounced degradation, and outlines governance mechanisms for critical infrastructure and project management.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: La investigación titulada “El uso de ChatGPT y su impacto sobre las habilidades críticas del pensamiento en estudiantes universitarios de la región Puno, 2024” tuvo como propósito determinar si el uso de la inteligencia artificial, específicamente ChatGPT, se relaciona con el pensamiento crítico de los estudiantes universitarios de la región Puno. El estudio surge ante la incorporación acelerada de la inteligencia artificial en el ámbito educativo y la preocupación de que, si bien ChatGPT puede facilitar el acceso a información, apoyar la realización de tareas y proporcionar respuestas rápidas, su utilización excesiva podría disminuir la necesidad de que los estudiantes analicen, cuestionen, evalúen y resuelvan problemas de manera autónoma. En este sentido, los autores identificaron como problemática la limitada evidencia existente sobre la relación entre ChatGPT y las habilidades de pensamiento crítico en estudiantes universitarios de la región Puno, considerando que investigaciones previas habían abordado principalmente los efectos de la inteligencia artificial sobre procesos cognitivos y metacognitivos de manera general. El estudio se desarrolló bajo un enfoque cuantitativo, correspondiendo a una investigación empírica con estrategia asociativa y diseño correlacional de corte transversal, debido a que buscó examinar estadísticamente la relación entre las variables sin manipularlas y mediante la recolección de información en un momento determinado. La población estuvo conformada por estudiantes universitarios del departamento de Puno, provenientes de diferentes áreas académicas, y se planteó inicialmente una muestra de 500 estudiantes con edades principalmente comprendidas entre los 18 y 30 años; finalmente, participaron 512 estudiantes universitarios, de los cuales el 53.1 % fueron mujeres y el 46.8 % hombres. Asimismo, el 97.4 % manifestó conocer ChatGPT y el 97.2 % señaló haber utilizado esta herramienta. El muestreo empleado fue no probabilístico por conveniencia, por lo que los resultados deben interpretarse considerando las características específicas de los participantes y no como evidencia necesariamente generalizable a toda la población universitaria de Puno. Para evaluar la variable relacionada con ChatGPT se utilizó el Cuestionario de ChatGPT de Oros (2024), compuesto por 20 ítems organizados en las dimensiones de Fluidez, Flexibilidad y Originalidad, con respuestas en una escala Likert de cinco niveles; el instrumento presentó una consistencia interna global de α = .830 y ω = .829. Para evaluar el pensamiento crítico se empleó un cuestionario de 34 ítems compuesto por seis dimensiones: Interpretación, Análisis, Inferencia, Evaluación, Explicación y Autorregulación, cuya consistencia interna global alcanzó α = .902 y ω = .902. El procesamiento estadístico se realizó mediante JASP, utilizando estadísticos descriptivos, análisis de asimetría y curtosis, prueba de normalidad de Kolmogórov-Smirnov y el coeficiente Rho de Spearman para analizar la relación entre las variables. Los resultados mostraron que la percepción de ChatGPT fue predominantemente favorable, debido a que el 76.5 % de los participantes presentó una percepción buena y el 12.8 % una percepción muy buena; sin embargo, esta percepción positiva no implicó una relación significativa con el pensamiento crítico. El resultado principal evidenció una correlación prácticamente nula entre ChatGPT y el pensamiento crítico global (Rho = −.010; p = .830), por lo que no se encontró evidencia estadísticamente significativa de una asociación entre ambas variables. Del mismo modo, al analizar las dimensiones específicas del pensamiento crítico, tampoco se encontraron relaciones estadísticamente significativas con ChatGPT: Interpretación (Rho = −.047; p = .291), Análisis (Rho = −.055; p = .218), Inferencia (Rho = .035; p = .430), Evaluación (Rho = −.016; p = .711), Explicación (Rho = .041; p = .357) y Autorregulación (Rho = −.030; p = .498). Aunque se identificó una asociación estadísticamente significativa entre la dimensión de Fluidez de ChatGPT y la dimensión de Inferencia del pensamiento crítico (Rho = .090; p = .042), su magnitud fue muy baja y constituye un resultado específico entre dimensiones, por lo que no modifica el resultado general de ausencia de relación significativa entre las variables principales. En la discusión, los autores plantean que ChatGPT puede constituir una herramienta útil para facilitar el acceso a información, apoyar actividades académicas, generar ideas y permitir la exploración de diferentes perspectivas; no obstante, también señalan que un uso excesivamente dependiente podría representar un riesgo para procesos como el análisis, la evaluación y la autorregulación del aprendizaje. Sin embargo, es importante precisar que tales riesgos corresponden principalmente a planteamientos teóricos y antecedentes discutidos en el artículo, ya que los datos obtenidos en esta investigación no demostraron una relación estadísticamente significativa entre el uso de ChatGPT y un aumento o disminución del pensamiento crítico. Entre las principales limitaciones se reconoce que el diseño correlacional y transversal no permite establecer relaciones causales; además, el muestreo por conveniencia limita la generalización de los resultados, la investigación se concentró exclusivamente en estudiantes de la región Puno y se estudió únicamente ChatGPT, sin incorporar otras herramientas de inteligencia artificial que también podrían estar relacionadas con los procesos cognitivos de los estudiantes. En conclusión, la investigación encontró que, dentro de la muestra de 512 estudiantes universitarios analizada, el uso de ChatGPT no presentó una relación estadísticamente significativa con el pensamiento crítico global ni con sus dimensiones de interpretación, análisis, inferencia, evaluación, explicación y autorregulación, por lo que los resultados no permiten afirmar que ChatGPT mejore o deteriore el pensamiento crítico; únicamente indican que, bajo las condiciones, instrumentos, población y diseño empleados, no se encontró una asociación estadísticamente significativa entre ambas variables.
